title: Birth-phase (pre-launch) fingerprint record — one JSON object per line in data/birthphase/<launchpad>.jsonl
description: Shared across all launchpads (Pump.fun, LetsBonk, Raydium LaunchLab, Believe/Meteora DBC, Bags, Moonshot, Boop, Heaven, Daos.fun, StonksFun, Hooked, Zora, Clanker, Flaunch, four.meme, Flap, Pons and other Robinhood Chain pads, Virtuals Genesis/bonding). Times are Unix ms (UTC). Money in USD unless the field name says otherwise. Wallets are SHORT ids (first4..last4) — the same short id is the join key for repeat-buyer detection across launches and across libraries. A field that could not be measured is null and the reason goes in coverage.missing — never fill with guesses. Virtuals worker: emit the same top-level fields; Genesis points/pledges go in 'presale' and first Genesis buyers/pledgers go in first_buyers with kind='pledge' or 'genesis'. Extra pad-specific fields go in 'ext' (free-form object).

launchpad.description: canonical id = file name: pump.fun, letsbonk, raydium-launchlab, meteora-dbc (Believe/others), bags, moonshot, boop, heaven, daos.fun, stonkfun, hooked, zora, clanker, flaunch, four.meme, flap, pons, robinhood-other, virtuals, ...

sample_stratum.description: How the token entered the library. 'random' = uniform draw from ALL launches on the pad in a time window; 'random_graduates' = uniform draw from all graduations (migrations). These two are the only strata used for base rates / population re-weighting. Catalog/screener/listing strata are outcome-enriched or activity-filtered and must not be used alone for base rates.

created_ts.description: token/curve creation (or presale open) time, ms

graduation_ts.description: curve completion / migration / official launch; null if never (see phase)

phase.description: no_curve = launches straight into an AMM pool (Clanker/Zora/Flaunch etc.): the 'birth phase' is then the first hour of the pool

first_buyers.description: first N buys in time order (N up to 100)

wallet_age_d.description: days between the wallet's first-ever tx and this buy; null if not resolved

wallet_age_note.description: 'exact', 'lower_bound' (history longer than the page cap) or 'nonce' (EVM: outgoing tx count at buy)

fresh.description: wallet created <= 7 days before the buy (Solana) / nonce <= 3 at the buy (EVM)

presale.description: presale / pledge / Genesis phase (Virtuals Genesis, Daos.fun fundraise, etc.)

features.description: scalar features at end of birth phase (graduation or last observation). All optional/nullable.

fresh_cluster_max.description: largest group of fresh wallets that bought within the same 2 s with sizes within ±10%

repeat_early_buyers.description: how many of the first 20 buyers were also first-20 buyers in >= 2 OTHER launches in the library (filled at build time)

repeat_early_buyers_winners.description: ...of which appeared early in other launches that reached $1M

trajectory.description: time-normalised arc: one point per checkpoint (seconds after created_ts: 30,60,120,300,600,900,1800,3600,7200,10800,21600,43200,86400) up to observed time

t_to_100k_s.description: seconds from created_ts to first mcap >= $100K (null = never in observed window)

resolution.description: time resolution of milestone timing, e.g. 'trades' / '1h candles' / 'daily'

outcome.description: labels used by the matcher: reached_100k/1m/10m (bool or null if censored/unknown)

ext.description: pad-specific extras. ext.snap is what the matcher uses: {"<age_s>": snapshot} for ages 60,300,900,1800,3600,10800 s after created_ts, each snapshot computed ONLY from data up to that age: {age, mcap, mcap_prev (mcap at max(30, age/5) s), curve_pct (0-100 or null), graduated (bool), n_trades, n_buyers (unique), vol (USD), top10 (top-10 buyer share of buy USD), sell_share, med_buy (median USD of first-20 buys up to age), gini20, same_sec (share of first-20 buys sharing a second), fresh20 (fresh share of first-20, needs >=4 resolved), n_first, _w (short ids of first-20 buyers), dev_pct (% supply bought by dev at creation), first_buy_delay (s), repeat (filled at build)}. Any key may be null. Records without ext.snap are kept for coverage and repeat-buyer sets but are not matchable.
